title: Anagram check

idea.rule: Same letters isn't the same word — the COUNTS have to match too.
idea.detail: Two words are anagrams when they use exactly the same letters the same number of times. A set throws the counts away — {'b', 'o'} could be 'bo', 'boob' or 'bobb'. Sorting keeps every letter, so two anagrams sort into the identical list.

watch.code:
a, b = pair
same = sorted(a) == sorted(b)
print(same)

model_restatement: Say True if the two words use exactly the same letters, the same number of times.

clarify.question: Could the words be different lengths?
clarify.answer: They could — then they can't be anagrams.

clarify_fallback: Good question — assume the simple case.
blueprint: Take both words. Compare the letters each one uses. Print whether they match.
draft_code:
a, b = pair
same = set(a) == set(b)
print(same)

checkpoints.prompt: With the fix — after line 2, what is same?

why_line: set('boob') and set('bobb') are both {'b', 'o'} — a set keeps which letters, not how many, so the counts difference vanishes.

explain.rule: A set is a guest list with no headcount — 'boob' and 'bobb' both invite b and o, so they look like the same party.
explain.bridge: So what keeps every letter, repeats and all, so you can compare them?

fix.rule: sorted(word) keeps every letter in order — two anagrams sort into the identical list.

walk.gloss: Sort each word's letters, repeats kept, and compare.

fix.recommended:
a, b = pair
same = sorted(a) == sorted(b)
print(same)

alternatives.note: Count both words and compare the tallies — the hashmap way.

hints: A set forgets how many of each letter there were.

follow_up.recommended:

follow_up.fix_hint: Nothing to change — sorted catches the extra s vs the extra e.

one_liner: Same letters isn't the same word — the COUNTS have to match too.
